issues.description: Ingest clears warnings/stats but never clears results, so deleted input rows remain in the database forever.
Harness B JSONL parsing assumes every JSON value is an object; arrays/scalars crash ingest with AttributeError.
Missing Harness B id/model/benchmark fields are accepted as empty strings, causing silent overwrites under duplicate empty keys.
Malformed Harness C XML raises ParseError and aborts ingest instead of recording a validation warning.
Untrusted XML is parsed with stdlib ElementTree without defusedxml or equivalent hardening against entity-expansion DoS.
Ingest commits row-by-row, so a mid-run failure can leave a partially refreshed database.
Harness A validates score/timestamp but not required identifiers like run_id, model, or task.
Epoch unit detection uses a brittle threshold that mishandles microsecond or nanosecond epoch values.
Timestamp parsing rejects otherwise valid ISO-8601/RFC3339 values with offsets or fractional seconds.
Harness A metadata accepts any JSON type, producing inconsistent raw_extra shapes despite metadata being described as structured extra data.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the requested directory without guardrails.
Tests cover planted happy-path quirks but miss stale-row behavior, malformed JSONL/XML, missing IDs, and partial-ingest failure modes.
